title: The Immutability of God
definition: The immutability of God means that God does not change in His being, character, promises, purposes, truth, or faithfulness.
summary: God is not unstable, uncertain, moody, or changeable like human beings. His character remains perfect, His Word remains trustworthy, and His purposes cannot fail.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. In Him, believers see the unchanging faithfulness of God toward sinners who need mercy, grace, forgiveness, and hope.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: God never changes. His holiness does not weaken, His love does not fail, His promises do not expire, and His truth does not shift with time.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: A changing god could not be trusted. Because the true God does not change, believers can rest in His promises and depend on His character in every season.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Anchor your faith in God's unchanging character. When life feels unstable, remember that the Lord remains faithful, true, holy, merciful, and sovereign.
